newsitem.title: UK: Russia, Brazil lead London emerging debt skywards.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Brazil lead London emerging debt skywards.

text.p: The prospect of landmark bond issues from Russia and Brazil drove the London emerging debt market higher with dealers reporting gains across the entire spectrum.
"Russia's up again another point and Brazil's very strong," said one trader at a major U.S. firm in London. "In Russia its on anticipation of roadshows for the Eurobond."

Dealers have barely been able to contain their enthusiasm for the east European giant's credit since the major rating agencies awarded it high speculative grade foreign currency debt ratings earlier this week.
The move clears the way for the launch of the country's first Eurobond issue, an expected $300 to $500 million deal to be lead managed by JP Morgan and SBC Warburg by early November.
While dates for the likely roadshows have not yet been announced, prices have been strengthening in anticipation.
Russian dollar Vnesh loans RUVNUSLNS=RR climbed one point to 80-1/4 in early trading, and MinFins 3 and 4 also firmed, though one east European debt trader said he thought prices might start to ease.
"We're starting to see some profit-taking at these levels," he said.
One analyst at a European firm here said the price talk on the forthcoming Eurobond was changing by the day.
"Every day the spread talk gets tighter and tighter," he said, adding market talk put it around 350 or even 300 basis points over Treasuries after 400-450 bp over before the ratings.
He said Swiss franc-denominated Vnesh paper RUVNCHLNS=RR in particular still had considerable upside. It was quoted at 77-1/2 on screen.
"Swiss franc Vnesh is going to trade closer to Mexican and Argentine spreads on average -- there is still over 20 points to go," he said. "The upside is still fairly frightening."
The other twin motor of the morning's trade came from Brazil, as rumours it is due for a rating upgrade spun round the marketplace.

Although Standard & Poor's and Moody's both declined to comment on the market talk, Brady bond dealers said the prospect of an upgrade could explain the seemingly delayed launch of the country's forthcoming global bond.
Dealers have been waiting for two weeks for the issue to come to market. They are expecting a $750 million to $1.0 billion five-year deal and say an upgrade would give it a big boost.
Moody's currently rates Brazil B1 while S&Ps classes it B-plus with a positive outlook.

Rumours of the upgrade, and anticipation of its bond, drove Brazilian prices higher during the morning. Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR climbed 1/2 point to 73-3/4, and pulled the other Latin credits up with it.
Venezuelan DCBs VZFLL07=RR gained about 1/4, rising to 84-3/4 bidside, amid the generally bullish market tone.
Even Bulgaria's inexorable fall was halted early in the session after its central bank intervened to help the embattled lev.
Bulgarian FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were steady at 34-00. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
